
##### Homogeneous network interference

We now introduce the **assumption of homogeneous network interference**, which reduces the complexity of network exposure mappings.  This assumption holds that for any node \(i\) in the network, the effect of a neighbor’s treatment is the same regardless of which neighbor it is, and regardless of the position of unit \(i\) in the network.  Under this assumption, network exposure mappings are further restricted so that their values lie in a finite set.

The result of these assumptions is a model we call the **Network Fully Randomized Causally Interpretable Structured Tree Graph (NFFRCISTG)** — a structured approach to reasoning about interventions in networks.  In the section below, we derive an NFFRCISTG model for [Example 2](#sec-example-2), illustrating its central assumption using the corresponding structural equations.
